peak.name: The Peak
peak.summary: Views across the city and Victoria Harbour. Public viewing areas, paid observation decks and the Peak Tram are separate experiences.
peak.tip: Expect slopes. Visibility, tickets, transport and access should be checked before departure.

tai-kwun.name: Tai Kwun
tai-kwun.summary: A heritage and arts centre in the restored Central Police Station compound, combining historic buildings, cultural activities and contemporary art.
tai-kwun.tip: Indoor galleries and outdoor courtyards have different access arrangements. Check exhibition and tour schedules.

pmq.name: PMQ
pmq.summary: Former police married quarters adapted into a creative hub with local design shops and craft studios. Combine it with Tai Kwun and a Central neighbourhood walk.
pmq.tip: Shop and event hours vary. Outdoor corridors may be exposed to wind and rain.

man-mo.name: Man Mo Temple
man-mo.summary: A declared monument on Hollywood Road, preserving traditional temple architecture and historic objects. Combine it with the streets of Sheung Wan and Central.
man-mo.tip: Respect worshippers and on-site photography rules. Incense smoke can be strong.

escalator.name: Central–Mid-Levels Escalator
escalator.summary: The escalator system links Central and the Mid-Levels, passing streets, shops and cultural spaces. It can form part of a neighbourhood walk.
escalator.tip: The escalators do not run in both directions at once. Check direction and service signs; the return trip may involve walking.

lan-fong-yuen.name: Lan Fong Yuen, Central
lan-fong-yuen.summary: A longstanding eatery on Gage Street, known for Hong Kong-style milk tea and cha chaan teng dishes such as pork chop buns.
lan-fong-yuen.tip: The listed address is 2 Gage Street, Central. Confirm menus, prices, hours and queues with the restaurant.

avenue-stars.name: Avenue of Stars
avenue-stars.summary: A harbourfront promenade celebrating Hong Kong cinema, with views of the Hong Kong Island skyline. Suitable for an easy walk and photography.
avenue-stars.tip: This is an outdoor waterfront. Bring sun protection. The source does not confirm any light show or fireworks.

star-ferry.name: Star Ferry, Tsim Sha Tsui
star-ferry.summary: The Star Ferry is a classic way to experience Victoria Harbour. This record represents the Tsim Sha Tsui ferry pier.
star-ferry.tip: The itinerary only schedules a pier visit. Sailings, fares and routes must be checked separately; no ticket is booked.

hkmoa.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
hkmoa.summary: The museum on Salisbury Road presents Chinese antiquities, painting and calligraphy, export art, and modern and Hong Kong art.
hkmoa.tip: Exhibitions rotate. Confirm opening days, closures and special exhibition charges on the official website.

art-park.name: West Kowloon Art Park
art-park.summary: Public park and waterfront space in the West Kowloon Cultural District, offering harbour views near M+ and the Hong Kong Palace Museum.
art-park.tip: The park and museums are separate visits. Outdoor activities depend on the weather.

mplus.name: M+
mplus.summary: A museum of modern and contemporary visual culture, including visual art, design, architecture and moving images. Combine it with the West Kowloon waterfront.
mplus.tip: Check the official website for exhibition tickets, reservations and closure days. This project does not provide live ticketing.

palace-museum.name: Hong Kong Palace Museum
palace-museum.summary: A museum presenting Chinese art and culture and encouraging exchange between civilisations, in the West Kowloon Cultural District.
palace-museum.tip: Exhibitions, tickets and closure days can change. Confirm them on the official museum website.

knutsford.name: Knutsford Terrace
knutsford.summary: A dining neighbourhood with international restaurants and bars. This is an area recommendation, rather than a restaurant reservation.
knutsford.tip: Menus and hours vary by business. Compare nearby options against your budget.

temple-street.name: Temple Street
temple-street.summary: A neighbourhood associated with street markets and local food, including claypot rice. It can be considered for an evening visit.
temple-street.tip: Stall hours vary. The project does not promise that any particular stall will be open.

hing-kee.name: Hing Kee Restaurant
hing-kee.summary: An eatery featured in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's Temple Street food guide, known for claypot rice and oyster omelettes.
hing-kee.tip: Consider it as a dinner option. Confirm menus, prices, seating and opening hours with the business.

sham-shui-po.name: Sham Shui Po
sham-shui-po.summary: Traditional shops, fabric and craft-material streets, independent cafes and local eateries offer a look at everyday neighbourhood life.
sham-shui-po.tip: This record describes a neighbourhood, not a specific shop. Arrange shopping and meals according to on-site conditions.

hop-yik-tai.name: Hop Yik Tai
hop-yik-tai.summary: An eatery on Kweilin Street known for Hong Kong-style rice rolls, suitable for a snack stop during a neighbourhood walk.
hop-yik-tai.tip: The listed address is 121 Kweilin Street. Confirm menus and opening arrangements. A snack stop is not a full lunch.

nan-lian.name: Nan Lian Garden and Chi Lin Nunnery
nan-lian.summary: Adjacent garden and nunnery with Tang-style architecture, landscaped grounds and a quiet setting for traditional culture and garden visits.
nan-lian.tip: Respect religious and photography rules. Garden paths may be slippery in rain.

big-buddha.name: Big Buddha and Po Lin Monastery
big-buddha.summary: A prominent religious and cultural site on Lantau Island, near Po Lin Monastery. Visiting the Buddha involves steps; choose a route suited to your fitness.
big-buddha.tip: Stair access and indoor visits may have different arrangements. Check mountain transport and weather before departure.

ngong-ping.name: Ngong Ping Village
ngong-ping.summary: A village setting on Lantau Island that can be combined with the Big Buddha and Po Lin Monastery, with natural scenery and cultural attractions nearby.
ngong-ping.tip: Ngong Ping 360 is a paid transport experience, separate from a village walk. Check maintenance, weather and transport arrangements.

tai-o.name: Tai O
tai-o.summary: A fishing village known for stilt houses and local snacks. It can be combined with Ngong Ping, with additional transport between the two areas.
tai-o.tip: Straight-line distances are not road distances. Allow extra time for weekend traffic and queues.

hk-park.name: Hong Kong Park
hk-park.summary: An urban park with ponds, aviary space and the Flagstaff House Museum of Tea Ware, offering a break between Central and Admiralty.
hk-park.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

zoological-gardens.name: Hong Kong Zoological and Botanical Gardens
zoological-gardens.summary: A historic urban park with gardens, a greenhouse and bird and animal displays, extending a Central walk into green space.
zoological-gardens.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

kowloon-park.name: Kowloon Park
kowloon-park.summary: An urban park amid the busy streets of Tsim Sha Tsui, with a Chinese garden and comic character sculptures.
kowloon-park.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

victoria-park.name: Victoria Park
victoria-park.summary: Open green and recreational space for a break between shopping areas. Seasonal events require separate confirmation.
victoria-park.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

blue-house.name: Blue House Cluster
blue-house.summary: Historic tenement buildings on Stone Nullah Lane. The Blue, Yellow and Orange Houses reflect neighbourhood life and architectural conservation; the Hong Kong House of Stories is on the Blue House ground floor.
blue-house.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

pak-tai-wanchai.name: Pak Tai Temple Wan Chai
pak-tai-wanchai.summary: A historic temple also known as Yuk Hui Kung. Its Pak Tai statue and traditional architecture provide an introduction to local religious culture.
pak-tai-wanchai.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

science-museum.name: Hong Kong Science Museum
science-museum.summary: Interactive exhibits introduce mechanics, sound, light, electromagnetism and environmental science through hands-on activities.
science-museum.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

space-museum.name: Hong Kong Space Museum
space-museum.summary: A domed waterfront landmark with astronomy and space science exhibitions and a planetarium. Consult its website for programme and visiting arrangements.
space-museum.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

clock-tower.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Clock Tower
clock-tower.summary: The red-brick and granite tower of the former Kowloon-Canton Railway terminus is a historic waterfront landmark, viewed from the surrounding public space.
clock-tower.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

goldfish-market.name: Goldfish Market
goldfish-market.summary: A distinctive market on northern Tung Choi Street, with aquarium and pet shops. Respect shop rules and avoid flash photography.
goldfish-market.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

flower-market.name: Mong Kok Flower Market
flower-market.summary: A flower retail and wholesale neighbourhood around Mong Kok and Prince Edward, suitable for observing local florists and garden culture.
flower-market.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.

ladies-market.name: Ladies Market
ladies-market.summary: A street market around Tung Choi Street with clothing, daily goods and small accessories, offering a busy street-shopping atmosphere.
ladies-market.tip: Check the official source for visiting areas, opening arrangements and events. Coordinates and suggested visit durations are approximate planning assumptions.
